file_name: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.txt

barriers.description: The COVID-19 pandemic severely limited access to and communication with relevant user groups, reducing opportunities for in-person engagement and participant availability.
barriers.justification: This resource constraint directly hindered the team's ability to facilitate user involvement and to manage a deep, evolving understanding of users (e.g., through longitudinal or on-site engagement), which affected user research and evaluation activities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Another constraint is the currently active COVID-19 pandemic, which leads to severe limitations in the availability and communication ability of the relevant user groups, especially in Africa.

barriers.description: Intercontinental and intercultural communication between the German development team and on-site user groups posed challenges due to differences in culture and distance.
barriers.justification: This interactional knowledge gap impeded managing user understanding and made it harder to plan and maintain valid participatory evaluation methods and accurate contextual inquiry across cultures.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The particular challenge in this project is the intercontinental and intercultural communication with the user groups on-site since the development team consists of German physicians and computer scientists.

barriers.description: Language limitations required the use of interpreters (French/Malagasy to English), reducing direct communication between designers and users.
barriers.justification: Relying on interpreters limited designers' ability to capture nuanced user insights and hindered facilitation of user involvement and the fidelity of participatory evaluations.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Interviews were conducted in English, French, and Malagasy. Interpreters translated from French to English or Malagasy to English when necessary.

barriers.description: Socio-cultural power dynamics and hierarchies led some participant groups to withhold honest expression unless settings were adapted (e.g., gender-homogenized or smaller groups).
barriers.justification: These trust and power issues restricted genuine user participation and expression, undermining the team's ability to facilitate user involvement and to obtain authentic user understanding needed for accurate requirement specification.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Due to the cross-cultural characteristics of the region, a deliberate attempt for specific user groups was made to reduce the number of participants and homogenize by gender; otherwise, some of the evaluation participants may not express themselves honestly or at all.

barriers.description: The team was unable to conduct desired on-site observations because of the global COVID-19 pandemic.
barriers.justification: Lack of on-site observation prevented designers from fully understanding the context of use and real-world workflows, constraining requirements elicitation and realistic evaluation of prototypes.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Since user behavior plays a crucial role in any technology, we wished to conduct additional on-site observations during the analysis and evaluation phases. Unfortunately, this was not possible due to the global COVID-19 pandemic.

barriers.description: Stable IT infrastructure and Internet connectivity were only partially available in primary health care facilities, limiting how the system could be used and tested in situ.
barriers.justification: Limited connectivity constrained realistic evaluation and understanding of the context of use (e.g., offline behavior, upload workflows), and restricted designers' ability to evaluate prototypes under true operating conditions.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Stable IT infrastructure was only partially present in primary health care facilities. After Marie has finished her work, she stays at the Community Health Center for a while to upload the pictures taken that day via the AINA application since she does not have an Internet connection at home.

barriers.description: Application of AI/medical device guidelines to the documentation kept technical terminology, which users found difficult to understand.
barriers.justification: Regulatory-driven or guideline-driven documentation requirements limited designers' ability to simplify language for users, hindering efforts to address holistic user experience and manage user understanding during iteration.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Unfortunately, the revision of the manual, based on AI guidelines for medical devices, did not reduce the number of technical terms used, so all users commented negatively on this.
